Scope: .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh, .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh + AGENTS.md (Prime Directive 11, the rule this hook enforces — read, unchanged), .claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.sh (read only to confirm the sibling finding in ③)

Read: card #24812 (body and both comments), PR #24886 (body, file list, net diff against merge-base `b1676441b` — byte-identical to the API diff apart from `index` abbreviation; `main` has not touched `.claude/hooks/` since that base), both files whole at the head, and the 40 check-runs on the head (read 2026-10-20T13:25Z; every one `completed`).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each traced by hand through `subst_end()` and the three scanners at the head:

1. A read whose double-quoted word holds a `$(…)` or backtick body containing its own quotes and a greater-than sign: BLOCK → ALLOW. Right — this is the card's defect (table rows 1 and 2, the original multi-line probe, and the backtick spelling). Pinned by the three `allow` cases in the new self-test section.
2. The fail-open mirror — one `"` inside such a body used to leave the outer string hanging, so a real `sed -i` behind a separator rode through as text: ALLOW → BLOCK. Right — recall is gained, not lost. Pinned (`printf '"'` case, plus its nested form).
3. The heredoc delimiter scan (`strip_line_comment`) — a blank-then-hash inside such a body used to truncate the introducing line, dropping the real heredoc introducer so the body lines were read as commands (a false block): BLOCK → ALLOW. Right; pinned. The card named two quote-aware passes; the hook has three readers of the same rule, and leaving the third would be a third dialect — the #11131 lesson the card itself cites.
4. A write INSIDE a quoted `$(…)` (`echo "$(sed -i s/a/b/ pkg/x.ts)"`): ALLOW → ALLOW. Unchanged in verdict, now named in the header's fail-open list and pinned in the "deliberately does NOT claim" section. Right — it is the wrapped-invocation class the header already fails open on, and the UNQUOTED form still blocks.
5. Recall beside a quoted substitution — a redirect after the closing quote, a write behind a semicolon preamble, a `sed -i` script holding `$(date +%F)`: BLOCK → BLOCK. Right; these three pins are exactly what makes the dispatch-suggested fail-open route go red, which is the measured reason the dev took the card's route 1 instead.
6. The nested pin (`"$(echo "$(printf '"')")"` then a semicolon and a real `sed -i`) is discriminating: without the helper's nested-`$(` arm the inner `"` pops the stack early, the rest of the command is swallowed as inert, and the write is missed. My trace agrees with the dev's per-site ablation.
7. The boundary the helper introduces, stated in its header: a `(` or `)` bash would not count — a `case` pattern, a paren inside a comment within the body — moves the end. Too early, and the tail is read exactly as the pre-fix hook read it (traced: a `case` pattern inside the quoted body followed by a real redirect still blocks). Too late, and the swallowed tail is inert — a new fail-open on one rare shape (a multi-line comment holding an unbalanced paren inside a quoted substitution, followed by a real redirect). Judged right under the hook's declared PRECISION OVER RECALL contract; the header now states both directions, which is what the final comment-only commit added.
8. Arithmetic expansion `"$((1+2))"` followed by a real redirect is handled by paren balance and still blocks. A backslash-escaped `$(` or backtick inside the string is consumed by the pre-existing escape branch before the new branch runs in all three scanners, so it opens nothing — consistent with bash.
9. Public surface: none. `.claude/**` publishes nothing; the exit-code contract (0 allow, 2 block), the `OS_ALLOW_MAIN_EDITS=1` hatch, the refusal text and the jq-less fallback are untouched. The rule side, AGENTS.md Prime Directive 11 ("precision-first: it never blocks reads … any shape it cannot resolve with confidence … is allowed through"), needs no edit — the diff moves the hook toward it.
10. Self-test delta is +11 cases (10 in the new #24812 section, 1 in the fail-open section), matching the claimed 130 → 141; the file's pre-existing shape (hermetic fixture, pass/fail counters) is unchanged.
11. Bash 3.2 floor: the helper uses `${s:i:n}` with arithmetic offsets (a form the pre-fix scanners already use), `+=`, `${st%?}` and an arithmetic `for`; `st` is never empty when `top` is computed, because the function returns the moment it empties. `check:bash32-floor` runs inside the green Lint lanes.

Check-runs on the head, as read: the five required contexts — `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Test Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Build Core` **skipped** (paths-filtered; the `filter` job is success and a bash hook has no build leg — reported as the conclusion it is, not read as a pass). Every other non-skipped run is success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, the seven Lint lanes, the four Type Check lanes, Dogfood Regression Gate, and the three card-claim guards. No `in_progress`, no failure.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff is `.claude/hooks/**` only — no released package, no `skills/**`, no export, no schema — so nothing publishes, and `Check Changeset` is success. `Clause-②: no`, with no arm, on the PR body and on the dispatch agree, and it is right: the accept-set changes above are an internal-tooling bug fix with no published or authorable surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. The eight declared deviations, each answered:

- Route 1 (track the substitution as its own quoting context) instead of the dispatch-suggested route 2 (fail open on any double-quoted word holding `$(`): ACCEPTED. The card's Expected offers either; the dev measured route 2 against the pre-fix hook, found it lets three real writes through that the pre-fix hook blocks, and pinned all three so route 2 goes red. Prime Directive 5 over a smaller parser surface.
- The backtick spelling and the third scanner (heredoc delimiter scan) folded in: ACCEPTED — same defect class, same helper, each pinned by a discriminating case (judgments 3 and 6).
- The depth-2 nested allow pin replaced by a nested recall pin: ACCEPTED (judgment 6).
- Local builds of formula and lint to clear a gate prerequisite; extra gates run; `test:repo` not run (not derived, and `Test Core` is success on the head); the model-free commit trailer pair per AGENTS.md rather than the harness reminder's spelling: all ACCEPTED, none touches the diff. The three commits carry the `Claude-Session` trailer naming this seat session and the model-free co-author line.
- No objectui mirror PR and `guard-shared-stash.sh` untouched: ACCEPTED for this PR — both are outside the dispatch's declared file surface, which said stop on breach. ESCALATED to the seat as three findings the seat owns filing (Prime Directive 10: a reproducible defect with a named location is a card, not a note):
  1. `.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.sh` `split_segments()` carries the identical pre-fix in-double-quote branch and no `subst_end` (confirmed at this head: zero occurrences) — the same false block on `echo "a $(echo "x; git stash pop")"`. Family card, same fix shape.
  2. The objectui twins of both hooks. This hook's own header (lines 14–16, untouched by the diff) promises the two repos' copies are kept case-for-case identical; this PR knowingly diverges from that promise until the mirror lands, so the mirror card is the remedy and the header claim is stale meanwhile.
  3. The neighbouring shape — a double-quoted parameter expansion whose default value holds a nested quote and a greater-than sign — still false-blocks. Its quoting semantics differ from a substitution's, so it is not an extension of this helper: its own card.
- Cosmetic, no action: the PR body says "+77 / -1"; the net diff at this head is +78 / -1, the final comment-only commit having added one line after the body was written. The file list and the claimed scope are exact.

Tier and landing: `.claude/**` is the Tier S row of `GOVERNED_SURFACES`; the PR is draft, its head repo equals the base repo, its size is far under the 3,000-line ceiling, the dispatch `Claim:` names this branch, and the card-claim guards are success. With this PASS record on the head, the owning seat may land it through the queue; the seat reads the check-runs itself before arming.
